description: claim() is `whenNotPaused` but NOT `nonReentrant`. It calls _updatePool() then _claimRewards(msg.sender) which (a) `phUSD.mint(user, pendingPhUSDAmount)` and (b) `rewardToken.safeTransfer(user, pendingRewardAmount)` BEFORE rebasing `user.phUSDDebt`/`user.stableDebt` (rebase happens after the call, in claim() body). If either external call yields control to the user (ERC777-style hook, callback in `phUSD.mint`, or a non-standard reward token), the attacker re-enters `claim()` (or `withdraw`/`stake`) and reads the still-OLD `userDetails.phUSDDebt`/`stableDebt` from storage, re-minting/re-transferring the same pending amount until the user's pending hits zero or rewardBalance dries up. Matches REENTRANCY-ERC777: token interaction precedes critical state update, no reentrancy guard. Trust assumption guarding this finding is that phUSD is non-callback and rewardToken is a standard non-hooked stablecoin (per profile §10). Pattern-only match; reachability depends on cross-contract trust which is the code-scanner's call.
vulnerableConditionsMet: State changes (debt rebase) occur AFTER external token interaction
No nonReentrant on claim/stake/withdraw (only collectReward is guarded)
rewardToken type is not restricted by the contract
missingMitigations: CEI ordering (rebase debts BEFORE _claimRewards external calls)
Whitelist of trusted reward token implementations
